name: אֲבִירָם
summary: Two bearers. Abiram son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who with his brother Dathan joined Korah against Moses and Aaron, refused to come up when Moses called them, and went down alive into the grave when the earth opened (Num 16:1, 12–14, 27–33; 26:9–10; Deu 11:6; Psa 106:17). And Abiram the firstborn of Hiel of Bethel, at whose cost Jericho's foundation was laid, as Joshua had said (1Ki 16:34; Jos 6:26). The name is אָבִי “my father” with רָם “high, exalted”, a sentence like אֲחִירָם and אֲדֹנִירָם: “my father is exalted”, the father being God, as in Psa 89:27, “he shall call me, You are my father”.

evidence.note: “Korah … and Dathan and אֲבִירָם the sons of Eliab, and On … sons of Reuben.”
“Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram … and they said, We will not come up.”
The earth opened and they “went down alive into the grave (שְׁאֹלָה)”.
“The earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered the company of Abiram.”
“He laid its foundation בַּאֲבִירָם his firstborn … according to the word of Yahweh which he spoke by Joshua.”
“Yahweh in Zion is great, וְרָם הוּא above all the peoples”: the second element, said of God.
“He shall call me, אָבִי אַתָּה, my God and the rock of my salvation.”

note: BDB files the name under אָב (a.ae.av); the av entry leaves personal names in אֲבִי- to names/, and compound names are filed under their second element. Whether אָבִי here means God as father, or a kinsman, scripture does not say for this name; the reading “my father (God) is exalted” follows the parallel names with אֲחִי- and אֲדֹנִי-.
